children: Canada and China have agreed to expand trade cooperation, with Beijing providing tariff relief on approximately C$400M ($280M) of Canadian exports, including pork and seafood, as Prime Minister Mark Carney met Chinese President Xi Jinping ahead of the APEC summit.

Under the agreement, China will ease tariffs on Canadian agricultural and seafood products, while Canada will extend existing tariff-remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminum products by two years, through the end of 2028, Carney's office said.
Carney said Canada was ahead of schedule on its goal of increasing exports to China by 50% by the end of the decade. He described bilateral relations as more predictable and stable.

The meeting in Shenzhen marked the third time Carney and Xi have met since the Canadian leader took office. Xi said stronger communication and cooperation between the two countries would benefit both nations and the wider Asia-Pacific region.
The trade expansion comes as Canada seeks to diversify its export markets and reduce its reliance on the U.S., which has imposed tariffs on several Canadian products.
China has also recently extended tariff relief on Canadian canola meal, lobsters, crabs, and peas for two years, following earlier reductions in duties on Canadian canola seed.

title: Canada, China extend tariff relief measures through 2028
